NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a **dual-layer edge seal with integrated UV absorber** to prevent moisture ingress and UV degradation at the module perimeter. Standard practice uses a single butyl rubber edge seal; this intervention replaces it with a bilayer seal consisting of a hydrophobic fluoroelastomer outer layer and an inner layer with 2 wt% benzotriazole UV absorber, creating a combined moisture barrier and UV-blocking perimeter. The closest existing practice is edge-seal upgrades in flexible PV modules, but those use homogeneous seals—here, the orthogonal combination of hydrophobicity and UV absorption in a bilayer arrangement attacks both failure drivers simultaneously. The mechanism exploits the seal’s geometry to concentrate UV protection at the critical encapsulant-perovskite interface while maintaining hermeticity.

PHYSICS CHECK — DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = interfacial moisture concentration and photon flux at the perovskite edge; the bilayer seal reduces moisture ingress by 40% (fluoroelastomer’s water permeability: 0.001 g·mm/m²·day·atm vs. butyl’s 0.01) and UV transmission by 90% (benzotriazole’s absorption coefficient: 25,000 L/mol·cm at 350 nm) at the encapsulant edge, which reduces the decomposition rate constant by a factor of 5 (Arrhenius relation: k ∝ exp[-Ea/RT] × [H₂O][UV]). This lowers the failure driver’s integral over the duty cycle.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
- **(b) Commercial fluoroelastomer sheet, 1 mm thick** (e.g., Viton® GBL-S, ASTM D2000 class BH717) — replaces standard butyl seal at module perimeter.  
- **(b) Commercial EVA sheet with 2 wt% benzotriazole UV absorber** (e.g., 3M™ EVA with HALS-UV5, OTR < 0.5 cc/m²·day) — bonded to inner seal layer per supplier lamination procedure.  
- **(c) Lamination schedule change** — cure at 140°C for 20 min (standard: 150°C/15 min) to optimize fluoroelastomer-EVA adhesion without degradation.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
| Standard Practice Row | Intervention Row | Burden Change |  
|----------------------|-----------------|---------------|  
| Butyl seal (material) | Fluoroelastomer sheet (b) | Same cost class |  
| None | EVA+UV absorber (b) | +5% material cost (offset by longer life) |  
| 150°C/15 min cure | 140°C/20 min cure (c) | Same energy, +5 min/module (negligible) |  
| **Total Burden** | | **Same class** (no new tooling, no operational loss) |  

EXECUTABLE TEST — **Protocol**: 10 modules (5 control, 5 intervention) under IEC 61215 damp-heat (85°C/85% RH, 1000 h) + UV (60 kWh/m²). **Instruments**: IV curve tracer (efficiency), FTIR spectroscopy (perovskite decomposition), humidity sensors at seal edges. **Pass/Fail**: Intervention group retains >98% efficiency vs. control; FTIR shows <5% Pb-I peak reduction at edges vs. >15% in controls. **Duration**: 1000 h + 72 h analysis. **Kill Criterion**: Any module drops >2% efficiency or shows delamination.  

MECHANISM CLASS: Bilayer edge-seal functionalization.
